deleted_file_verdict.argument: The docket does not lie (it reports the ref as unresolved, and the docket's own claim is limited to what it holds), so this is a capability gap rather than a provenance falsehood. But it is a defect against the stated purpose: pinning exists to obtain the bytes that existed AT the commit, and deletion from the working tree is the extreme case of the working tree having moved on. The ref->request stage (_resolve_one) requires the path to exist on disk before pinning is attempted, so a citation that was verifiable at commit X silently loses its material whenever the file is later deleted -- and a deletion is exactly the scenario a commit-pinned docket is supposed to survive. The bytes are present in the object store and were never consulted.
deleted_file_verdict.recommended_fix: Resolve refs tree-first in commit mode: check the recorded commit's tree (git cat-file -t <commit>:<path>) BEFORE the on-disk existence test; materialize from the blob when the path exists at the commit, and keep not_a_file_in_target only for paths absent from BOTH the commit tree and the working tree. The mirror/refusal pipeline already accepts pinned-only sources, so this is a resolution-order change, not a new mechanism. Not fixed by V5.
